seo.title: Best Coffee Shops in Casablanca (2026) | tabiji.ai
seo.metaDescription: Discover Casablanca's best coffee shops, from traditional Moroccan cafes to modern specialty spots. Find top picks for ambiance, unique brews, and delicious pastries in 2026.

hero.subtitle: Casablanca's coffee scene is a vibrant blend of traditional Moroccan hospitality and emerging specialty coffee culture, offering everything from strong local brews to artisanal lattes.

picks.name: Boutique du Cafe
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Boutique du Cafe is a beacon for specialty coffee lovers in Casablanca. With a minimalist design and a focus on ethically sourced beans, they craft exquisite pour-overs and espresso-based drinks. It's a perfect spot for serious coffee drinkers and those seeking a quiet, sophisticated ambiance.
picks.insiderTip: Ask the barista about their current single-origin offerings; they often have rotating rare beans.
picks.redditQuote: "Boutique du Cafe is hands down the best place for a proper specialty coffee experience in Casa. Their flat white is consistently amazing."

picks.name: Blend Gourmand
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Blend Gourmand offers a delightful fusion of gourmet pastries, hearty brunch options, and excellent coffee. The vibrant atmosphere makes it a popular spot for both casual meet-ups and leisurely weekend meals. Their extensive menu ensures there's something for everyone, from sweet treats to savory dishes.
picks.whatToOrder: Caramel Macchiato with a 'Pain Perdu' (French Toast)
picks.insiderTip: Go early on weekends to avoid the brunch rush, especially if you want a window seat.
picks.redditQuote: "Can't recommend Blend Gourmand enough for brunch. Their coffee is strong and the pastries are out of this world."

picks.name: Pâtisserie Amoud
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A true Casablanca institution, Amoud is renowned for its exquisite Moroccan and French pastries, served alongside perfectly brewed coffee and traditional mint tea. The elegant setting and impeccable service provide a classic experience, perfect for indulging in sweet treats with your beverage.
picks.whatToOrder: Nos-Nos (Half-Half Coffee) with a selection of Moroccan petit fours
picks.insiderTip: Grab a box of their famed 'cornes de gazelle' to take home – they pair wonderfully with coffee.
picks.redditQuote: "You haven't truly experienced Casablanca until you've had coffee and pastries at Amoud. Their Nos-Nos is perfect."

picks.name: Oliveri
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Oliveri brings a taste of Italy to Casablanca with its classic Italian espresso, creamy gelato, and comfortable ambiance. It’s a popular spot for a quick caffeine fix or a relaxed afternoon treat. The quality of their coffee and desserts is consistently high, making it a reliable choice.
picks.whatToOrder: Classic Italian Espresso and a scoop of pistachio gelato
picks.insiderTip: They have fantastic seasonal gelato flavors; don't be afraid to try something new!
picks.redditQuote: "Oliveri makes the best cappuccino outside of Italy. Their gelato is a must-try too, especially in summer."

picks.name: The Coffee Factory
picks.whyItMadeTheList: As its name suggests, The Coffee Factory is all about the craft of coffee. This cafe doubles as a micro-roastery, offering freshly roasted beans and expertly prepared drinks in an industrial-chic setting. It's a favorite among local creatives and remote workers.
picks.whatToOrder: Cold Brew or a V60 pour-over with their latest roast
picks.insiderTip: You can buy freshly roasted beans to take home; the staff are knowledgeable and happy to advise.
picks.redditQuote: "If you're serious about your coffee, The Coffee Factory is the place to be. Their cold brew is strong and smooth."

picks.name: Paul
picks.whyItMadeTheList: This classic French bakery chain offers a reliable and enjoyable coffee experience. With its rustic French decor, Paul is perfect for a quick breakfast, a light lunch, or a coffee and pastry break. Their artisanal bread and viennoiseries are a highlight.
picks.whatToOrder: Latte with a freshly baked croissant
picks.insiderTip: Their baguettes are made fresh daily; grab one to accompany your coffee if you're planning a picnic.
picks.redditQuote: "Paul is always a safe bet for good coffee and an excellent croissant. I love their branch near the Twin Center."

picks.name: Maymana
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Maymana is synonymous with luxury and refined tastes in Casablanca. This upscale patisserie and cafe offers an array of meticulously crafted Moroccan and French pastries, served in a plush, elegant environment. It's ideal for a sophisticated coffee break or high tea.
picks.whatToOrder: Café au Lait with a selection of refined Moroccan pastries
picks.insiderTip: Their 'Makrout' (date-filled semolina pastries) are legendary and a must-try, especially with traditional mint tea.
picks.redditQuote: "Maymana is my go-to for special occasions. The ambiance is beautiful and their coffee and sweets are top-notch."

picks.name: Café La Sqala
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Set within the ancient ramparts of an 18th-century fortress, Café La Sqala offers an unparalleled traditional Moroccan coffee experience. Its lush garden courtyard provides a serene escape, perfect for enjoying strong Moroccan coffee and fresh breakfast. It's an iconic spot blending history with culinary delight.
picks.whatToOrder: Traditional Moroccan Coffee with a plate of Harcha (Moroccan semolina bread)
picks.insiderTip: Visit early in the morning for the most tranquil experience and to secure a prime spot in the courtyard.
picks.redditQuote: "Café La Sqala is more than a coffee shop, it's an experience. The historical setting and strong coffee are unforgettable."

picks.name: Starbucks Corniche
picks.whyItMadeTheList: For those seeking a familiar international coffee experience with an unbeatable view, Starbucks on the Corniche is a popular choice. Enjoy your favorite Starbucks beverage while overlooking the Atlantic Ocean. It's a convenient stop for tourists and locals alike.
picks.whatToOrder: Caramel Frappuccino with a panoramic ocean view
picks.insiderTip: The best time to visit is during sunset for spectacular views over the ocean while enjoying your drink.
picks.redditQuote: "It's a Starbucks, but the Corniche location has incredible ocean views that make it worth a visit. Great for people-watching."

picks.name: Le Gatsby
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Le Gatsby exudes a trendy, upscale vibe with its stylish decor and sophisticated menu. Beyond excellent coffee, they offer a range of gourmet sandwiches, salads, and desserts. It's a popular spot for business meetings, social gatherings, and those who appreciate a chic atmosphere.
picks.whatToOrder: Cortado and their famous Caesar Salad
picks.insiderTip: Their outdoor terrace is fantastic for enjoying the bustling Maârif neighborhood during cooler evenings.
picks.redditQuote: "Le Gatsby is super chic, great for a coffee meeting or just to feel a bit fancy. Their food is surprisingly good too."

picks.name: Pâtisserie Al Barakata
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Located in the charming Habous quarter, Al Barakata is a local favorite for authentic and affordable Moroccan pastries and coffee. It offers a glimpse into local life with its bustling atmosphere and a wide variety of traditional sweets. It’s perfect for a true taste of local Casablanca.
picks.whatToOrder: Moroccan Drip Coffee ('Qahwa Maghribia') with a 'Chebakia'
picks.insiderTip: This area is perfect for exploring after your coffee; you'll find artisan shops and traditional souks nearby.
picks.redditQuote: "Al Barakata in Habous is the real deal for cheap, delicious Moroccan pastries and strong coffee. Super authentic."

picks.name: La Croisée des Saveurs
picks.whyItMadeTheList: La Croisée des Saveurs is a cozy, boutique cafe known for its welcoming ambiance and carefully curated selection of French-inspired pastries and specialty coffees. It’s an ideal spot for a quiet moment, a quick catch-up with friends, or enjoying a good book.
picks.insiderTip: They often have unique seasonal tartlets; ask about the day's specials.
picks.redditQuote: "I love the chill vibe at La Croisée des Saveurs. Their coffee is good and the lemon tart is to die for!"

faq.question: What kind of coffee is popular in Casablanca?
faq.answer: Casablanca enjoys a diverse coffee culture. Traditional Moroccan coffee, often served strong and black or as 'Nos-Nos' (half coffee, half milk), is very popular. Additionally, espresso-based drinks like lattes and cappuccinos are widely available in modern cafes and international chains, catering to all preferences.

faq.question: Are there specialty coffee shops in Casablanca?
faq.answer: Yes, Casablanca has a growing specialty coffee scene. Places like Boutique du Cafe and The Coffee Factory are dedicated to sourcing high-quality beans, offering various brewing methods like pour-overs and cold brews, and providing an elevated coffee experience for connoisseurs.

faq.question: What is the typical price range for coffee in Casablanca?
faq.answer: The price for coffee in Casablanca varies. A traditional Moroccan coffee at a local cafe might cost 10-25 MAD ($1-2.50). At specialty coffee shops or international chains, a latte or cappuccino can range from 30-50 MAD ($3-5), with full meals or gourmet pastries increasing the total.

faq.question: Do coffee shops in Casablanca offer food options?
faq.answer: Absolutely. Most coffee shops in Casablanca, from traditional patisseries to modern cafes, offer a range of food options. This can include Moroccan pastries, French viennoiseries, light snacks, sandwiches, salads, and often full brunch menus, making them perfect for any meal.

faq.question: Are coffee shops in Casablanca suitable for working remotely?
faq.answer: Many modern coffee shops in Casablanca, particularly those in areas like Gauthier and Maârif, are well-suited for remote work. They often provide stable Wi-Fi, comfortable seating, and a quiet ambiance. However, it's always good practice to check if a specific cafe is typically busy during your intended visit.

faq.question: What's the best time to visit coffee shops in Casablanca?
faq.answer: Mornings are generally popular for breakfast and a quiet start to the day. Late afternoon (around 4-6 PM) is also a bustling time for coffee and pastry breaks, often referred to as 'goûter.' For a more relaxed experience, aim for mid-morning or early afternoon during weekdays.

methodology: Our selection of Casablanca's best coffee shops is based on extensive research, local recommendations, and consistent high ratings across various platforms. We prioritized venues offering exceptional coffee quality, unique atmosphere, excellent service, and value, ensuring a diverse list for every taste.
